audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] through whys[4] all end 'Cassiopeia' while win[1]-win[4] are 'Skill', and the whys are shifted one stage out of phase with their labels ('At 5' sits on the Level 6 row, 'By 6' sits on the First item row).
audit.why: Dr. Mundo wins 55.26% over 637 games and the mirror audit already set win[1]=Skill, win[2]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[5]/win[6]=Dr. Mundo; the why text has to state the same verdict as its side field.
audit.corrected: whys rewritten to close with Skill on rows 1-4 and Dr. Mundo on rows 5-6, each keyed to its own label.

audit.why: First item (MR/HP) and the two-item timing are already the stated flip points and they match the win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly claims Miasma's grounding 'denies your only gap-close' and that Dr. Mundo can 'E-stun' Cassiopeia. Dr. Mundo has no dash or movement ability and Blunt Force (E) applies no crowd control.
audit.why: Riot's text: Mundo Q is a ranged bonesaw, W is a self-aura, E is an auto-attack reset with bonus damage, R is heal plus move speed — nothing groundable and nothing that stuns. Miasma's slow is what actually hurts him. Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of damage dealt on a 0.75s cooldown, so Grievous Wounds is the real answer and was never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Grounding is irrelevant to Mundo — only the slow matters; Twin Fang heals every 0.75s so anti-heal decides extended fights; Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing her, so turning your back downgrades it to a slow.
sources: champ-data/_kits cassiopeia E text (0.75s cd, heal) and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing given against a champion whose entire sustain is Twin Fang lifesteal.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals a percentage of damage dealt on a 0.75s cooldown, so a single anti-heal source flips the attrition war.
